newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB details Prairie elevator space, railcar unload.
newsitem.headline: CWB details Prairie elevator space, railcar unload.

text.p: Vacant primary elevator space fell to 21 percent in the week ended April 13, while railcar unloads at export ports fell below targets, Canadian Wheat Board said.
Average vacancy in Prairie elevators was 21 percent compared to 25 percent April 7, CWB said.
Weather and equipment failure have delayed shipments of grains and oilseeds to Pacific ports since early January.
The effect has been a long backlog of vessels on the Pacific coast and more than C$20 million in demurrage fees against the CWB.
CWB filed a complaint to Canadian Transportation Agency Monday against Canadian National Railway and CP Rail System.

Manitoba elevators had the least space available at 16 percent versus 18 percent the week before, followed by Saskatchewan at 21 percent compared to 25 percent the prior week and then Alberta at 22 percent versus 27 percent the previous week.
Vancouver saw 2,788 railcars unloaded compared to the target of 3,300. The prior week saw 2,523 unloads. Prince Rupert unloaded 1,362 railcars compared to the target 1,300.
The last week saw 1,404 hopper cars unloaded in Prince Rupert.
Thunder Bay unloads totalled 1,224 railcars compared to the target of 1,750 hopper cars. The prior week saw 836 unloads.
